title: What changes when a second parity junction makes three fresh distinctions?
claim: Decide whether a source with all junction arities at most four and exactly two three-output additions forces its triple permissions against every reachable mixed-count rival. Isolate or eliminate a possible extra independent equation and report the exact scope if the argument widens.
standard_statement: For binary graphic cut spaces supplied by the specified serial rule, decide whether the pairwise minimum cocircuit cardinalities determine a marked three-coordinate extension when one source has vertex degree at most four and exactly two three-output additions.
prior_work: The one-sided short-equation theorem forces equality if at most one addition has three fresh outputs, using a sharp width-rank bound. The second extra output allows one additional independent check.
completion_gate: Prove an all-size decision for the stated two-three-fresh family or exhibit a full-table collision changing a three-parent choice.
source_contribution: Only the law, the current anonymous scalar table, and the three marks are supplied.

validation.status: Separate arguments, controls and full fixture replays passed within this task

conclusion: The truncated pair table identifies every ordinary junction up to the prescribed renaming. It determines all allowed states and every permitted one-, two- and three-parent choice. For two three-fresh additions the sharp horizon in bond-distance units is four. With three or more the sharp horizon is five for every exact count.
evidence_class: Uniform-family incidence theorem, sharp truncated-distance countermodels and independent finite-state certificates.
unrestricted_inverse_status: Open when both candidate presentations contain a junction with five or six distinctions. A full-table counterexample to three-parent eligibility still needs width at least 27.
failure_conditions: A reachable rival with a different physical junction but the same sufficiently truncated table as the stated source would refute the upper bound.
An invalid history, an unequal truncated entry, or equivalent actual verdicts in a matched lower-bound pair would invalidate sharpness for its count.
